item: a restored alternate stays with the law document it was recorded against, and a carried alternate is stored once per local document
summary: A backup holding one law document under two spellings (gbr and gb in an alpha-2 store) put an alternate recorded against one on the other, because the alternate's spelling was converted to the store's form first, and the duplicate check compared identity text, so a carried alternate was dropped from a sibling or stored twice depending on restore order. Now convert_alternate_countries leaves a law identity as recorded when the staged copy still holds that spelling at that url (restore only; kept_with_document reported when nonzero), the restore and the app place by one order (recorded spelling, store form, oldest document), and the law scope dedupes on (origin, fields, local row) with the held set read once per restore and an indexed temp table in the capture. 349 tests in the restore file, 495 across seven files on SQLite 3.45.1 and 3.53.1, 38 mutants killed. Limits: the same backup restored before and after the upgrade stores the alternate twice; legacy no-jurisdiction identities over siblings still differ between restore and app.
